The conservative nature of this increase indicates an expectation of continued stability rather than rapid acceleration.

The widening of the 90% confidence intervals as the time horizon extends directly reflects the increasing uncertainty inherent in longer-term forecasts. Essentially, the further out we project, the less certain we can be, as more variables and potential changes come into play.

While my forecast provides a central expectation and a range of likely outcomes, certain significant and unforeseen events could push the actual value beyond these stated intervals. On the upside, an unexpected major positive economic announcement, a groundbreaking technological advancement, a highly favorable regulatory decision, or a surprising corporate merger or acquisition could all trigger a sharp surge, potentially exceeding the upper bounds. Conversely, the downside risks include a sudden economic downturn or recession, the eruption of a major geopolitical conflict, a significant natural disaster, unexpected negative corporate earnings, or a systemic financial shock. Such events, by their very nature, are difficult to predict but possess the power to dramatically alter the trajectory of the forecasted value, pushing it well outside the 90% confidence levels for any given horizon.
